aaa_enabled.summary: Enable RADIUS authentication for centralized user management.
aaa_enabled.notes: Configure at least one RADIUS server before enabling. The default-group controls the privilege level for RADIUS-authenticated users. Ref: RouterOS User documentation - AAA.

secure_vty_transport.summary: Disable telnet and other cleartext management services; keep SSH and Winbox only.
secure_vty_transport.notes: Telnet (port 23) and FTP (port 21) transmit credentials in cleartext. HTTP (www) is unencrypted. Disable all cleartext services and use SSH or Winbox for management. Ref: RouterOS Securing your router.

vty_idle_timeout.summary: Set user inactivity timeout to 10 minutes or less with logout policy.
vty_idle_timeout.notes: The inactivity-timeout accepts RouterOS time format (e.g. 5m, 10m). The inactivity-policy must be set to 'logout' for the timeout to disconnect idle sessions. Default timeout is 10m but default policy is 'none' (no action). Ref: RouterOS User documentation.

enable_secret_encrypted.summary: RouterOS always stores passwords hashed. Ensure strong-crypto is enabled for SSH.
enable_secret_encrypted.notes: RouterOS does not have a separate enable secret; all user passwords are stored hashed. Enable strong-crypto for SSH to enforce modern ciphers. Ref: RouterOS SSH documentation.

no_default_snmp_community.summary: Change the default SNMP community name from 'public' to a unique string.
cli: /snmp community set [find default=yes] name=<UNIQUE-COMMUNITY> addresses=<MGMT-SUBNET>/24 security=private authentication-protocol=SHA1 encryption-protocol=AES authentication-password=<AUTH-PASS> encryption-password=<PRIV-PASS>
no_default_snmp_community.notes: The default community 'public' should be renamed. Use SNMPv3 security (security=private for authPriv) with address restrictions. Ref: RouterOS SNMP documentation.

no_write_snmp_community.summary: Disable write access on all SNMP communities.
no_write_snmp_community.notes: SNMP write-access allows remote configuration changes. Disable it on all communities. Ref: RouterOS SNMP documentation.

http_server_disabled.notes: The HTTP (www) service on port 80 transmits management traffic in cleartext. Use HTTPS (www-ssl) or Winbox instead. Ref: RouterOS IP Services documentation.

ssh_version_2.summary: RouterOS SSH is always version 2. No action required.
cli: # RouterOS SSH is natively version 2; no action required.
ssh_version_2.notes: RouterOS only supports SSH protocol version 2. Ref: RouterOS SSH documentation.

management_acl.summary: Restrict management services to authorized management subnet.
management_acl.notes: The address property on each IP service restricts which source IPs can connect. Connections from addresses outside this list are dropped before authentication. Ref: RouterOS IP Services documentation.

logging_enabled.summary: Configure remote syslog logging for audit trail.
cli: /system logging action add name=remote_syslog target=remote remote=<SYSLOG-IP> remote-port=514
logging_enabled.notes: Configure at least one remote syslog server. Add logging rules for relevant topics. RouterOS logs to memory by default but remote logging provides an audit trail. Ref: RouterOS Log documentation.

ntp_configured.summary: Enable NTP client and configure time servers.
ntp_configured.notes: At least two NTP servers should be configured for redundancy. NTP client is disabled by default. Ref: RouterOS NTP documentation.

login_banner.summary: Configure a login banner with an authorized-use notice.
cli: /system note set show-at-login=yes note="Authorized access only. All activity is monitored and logged."
login_banner.notes: The system note is displayed at each login when show-at-login=yes. Ref: RouterOS System Note documentation.

password_min_length.summary: RouterOS does not enforce password minimum length natively. Use strong passwords and RADIUS.
cli: # Configure password policies on the RADIUS server.
password_min_length.notes: RouterOS has no built-in password policy enforcement. Use RADIUS/TACACS+ for centralized password policy. Ref: RouterOS User documentation.

password_expiration.summary: RouterOS does not enforce password expiration natively. Use RADIUS for password lifecycle.
cli: # Configure password expiration on the RADIUS server.
password_expiration.notes: RouterOS has no built-in password expiration. Use RADIUS for centralized password lifecycle management. Ref: RouterOS User documentation.

lockout_configured.summary: RouterOS does not have native account lockout. Use firewall rules to rate-limit login attempts.
cli: /ip firewall filter add chain=input protocol=tcp dst-port=22 connection-state=new src-address-list=bruteforce action=drop
/ip firewall filter add chain=input protocol=tcp dst-port=22 connection-state=new action=add-src-to-address-list address-list=bruteforce address-list-timeout=10m
lockout_configured.notes: RouterOS does not have built-in account lockout. Use firewall address lists to block repeated login failures. Ref: RouterOS Securing your router.
